answers.explanation: Carrier sense multiple access: listen before transmitting.
A signal takes time to cross the cable, so a far node can hear silence after another has already started.
Both nodes keep sending to the end. CSMA/CD fixes that by aborting early.
Collision detection cuts the wasted time short.
Easy on a wire, hard on radio: your own signal drowns out the others at your antenna. That's why WiFi uses CSMA/CA.
A short jam signal makes sure every node knows a collision happened.
After the mth collision, K comes from {0, ..., 2^m - 1}: 2^3 - 1 = 7.
64 bytes, the minimum frame size. A frame must last long enough for the sender to hear about a collision.
Collision avoidance: random waits, and an ACK so the sender knows the frame got through.
Each host has its own link to a switch port, and full duplex means both directions at once, so there's nothing to collide with.
